reviewNote: Our current take for agentic coding across the major labs. S splits into Frontier, the most capable models for hard work, and Chores, the best value for routine work. Same-tier order is editorial, not a measured gap. Models reviewed but not shown are listed in notShown with the reason.

models.name: Opus 5.5

points.text: Coding-agent index: 62, the best; Sonnet 5.5 scores 59.
FrontierCode merge-ready code test: 46.4%, to Fable 5.2’s 49.1%.

models.rationale: S Frontier and the leader: first in Agent Arena on Arena’s Nov 4 board (+20.0%, 3.5 points ahead of #2 Gemini 4 Carbon, which is not generally available, and 4.6 ahead of #3 Sonnet 5.5) and first on AA’s Coding Agent Index v2.0 (61.7; Gemini 4 Carbon scored 59 on Oct 28). Fable 5.2 beats it on AA’s Intelligence Index v5 (65 vs 59) and FrontierCode 2.0 (49.1% vs 46.4%) but is not rated in Agent Arena yet and costs about 2.6 times as much per Intelligence Index task; see leadCheck. On Nov 9 every card moved to Arena’s Nov 4 board and every FrontierCode point to FrontierCode 2.0, from AA’s Fable 5.2 breakdown, which covers every shown model but Gemini 4 Argon. Theo’s audit (8.40, the best) and FrontierCode 1.1 (52.2%, the best) left Opus’s four posts to make room for AA’s Fable 5.2 thread.

leadCheck.note: Still #1 in Agent Arena; Fable 5.2 not rated yet.
leadCheck.reason: Fable 5.2 (Nov 9) leads Opus 5.5 on AA’s Intelligence Index v5 (65 vs 59) and FrontierCode 2.0 (49.1% vs 46.4%) and ties it on Terminal-Bench 4.0 (60%); Opus 5.5 leads on AA-Briefcase (1800 vs 1785 Elo, within the confidence interval) and costs about 2.6 times less per Intelligence Index task ($10.0 vs $26.5). Agent Arena has not rated Fable 5.2 yet (x.com/arena/status/2119882304718069874, “scores coming soon”); Opus 5.5 is #1 on its Nov 4 board. Anthropic itself recommends starting with Opus 5.5 for most coding. One evaluator’s launch-day run does not converge, so the leader holds until Agent Arena rates Fable 5.2. Gemini 4 Carbon (Oct 28) also challenged: #1 on AA’s Intelligence Index v5 at its launch (59, now 60) and #2 in Agent Arena (+16.5%), but behind Opus 5.5 there and on AA’s Coding Agent Index (59 vs 62), and not generally available, so not shown. The earlier challengers, Muse Wonder Full and Gemini 4 Argon, trail by 10.4 and 9.4 points in Agent Arena (Nov 4).

models.name: Fable 5.2

points.text: Intelligence Index: 65, the highest; Opus 5.5 scores 59.
Best on FrontierCode, a test of merge-ready code: 49.1%.
Costs 2.6× Opus 5.5 per Intelligence Index task at max effort.

models.rationale: S Frontier, second, entered Nov 9, the day it was released: AA’s Intelligence Index v5 puts it first at 65 (Gemini 4 Carbon 60, Opus 5.5 59, GPT-6 Astra 57), leading 5 of its 9 evaluations, and FrontierCode 2.0 first at 49.1% (high effort; max 48.8%) against Opus 5.5’s 46.4%. Placed after the incumbent leader, not first: the evidence is one evaluator’s launch-day run; Agent Arena has not rated it yet (“scores coming soon”, x.com/arena/status/2119882304718069874); it only ties Opus 5.5 on Terminal-Bench 4.0 (60%) and trails it on AA-Briefcase (1785 vs 1800 Elo); it costs about 2.6 times as much per Intelligence Index task ($26.5 vs $10.0); and Anthropic recommends starting with Opus 5.5 for most coding (anthropic.com/claude-fable-and-mythos-5-2). Its S seat took the spare slot from GPT-6 Astra. Anthropic’s own FrontierCode 2.0 chart (49.1% vs Opus 5.5’s 45.5%) and Vals’ index (71.31%, first) agree but are not X sources. Recheck at the next full Agent Arena board; move it, and the lead, only on converging evidence.

models.name: GPT-6.1 Sol

points.text: Coding-agent index: 54, to Opus 5.5’s 62, at a seventh of its cost.
Intelligence Index: 55, to Opus 5.5’s 59 and Fable 5.2’s 65.
FrontierCode merge-ready code test: 40.6%, to Opus 5.5’s 46.4%.

models.rationale: S Chores, the value pick: 54.1 on AA’s Coding Agent Index v2.0 at $1.50 a task, on its cost frontier between DeepSeek V4.1 Flash ($0.39) and GPT-6 Astra ($7.04 for 54.7), against Opus 5.5’s 61.7 at $11.42; #6 in Agent Arena at +12.5% (Max) on the Nov 4 board, at a $0.89 median cost per task against GPT-6 Astra’s $5.16 (x.com/arena/status/2115820547619926144); 55 on AA’s Intelligence Index v5. Weaker on FrontierCode 2.0 (40.6%, behind GPT-6 Astra’s 42.4% and GPT-6.1 Terra’s 42.3%) than on 1.1 (49.1%, at under a tenth of Opus 5.5’s cost per task), so the value case now rests on the coding-agent index and Agent Arena. Chosen over GPT-6.1 Terra (Oct 26), which is cheaper but trails it in Agent Arena (+10.9% vs +12.5%), on the Coding Agent Index (48 vs 54) and on the Intelligence Index (51 vs 55): mixed at best, so Sol stays. Not Frontier: Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.2 lead it in the same tests. On Nov 9 AA’s v5 posts replaced the FrontierCode 1.1 and Intelligence Index v4.3 posts, and every card moved to Arena’s Nov 4 board.

models.name: Muse Wonder Full

points.text: Coding-agent index: 59, to Opus 5.5’s 62 and GPT-6 Astra’s 55.
#6 in Code Arena WebDev, users’ votes on AI-built web apps.
Only in Meta’s Muse Code app; no public API.

models.rationale: A: converging independent results from AA (Coding Agent Index v2.0 58.9 in Muse Code, third behind Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5; Intelligence Index v5 50), Agent Arena (#9, +9.6% on Nov 4), Code Arena WebDev (#6, 1726 on Oct 19) and Theo’s audit (7.04). Behind Opus 5.5 in every reviewed head-to-head since v2.0 of AA’s coding index. First in A since Nov 9, when GPT-6 Astra left the chart. Gemini 4 Argon edges it in Agent Arena (+10.6% vs +9.6%) and ties it on the Intelligence Index (50), but trails it on the Coding Agent Index (53 vs 58.9) and Theo’s audit (3.95 vs 7.04): mixed, so Muse stays first. Usable only through Muse Code, with no per-token price yet.

models.name: Gemini 4 Argon

points.text: Hallucination rate: 4%, the lowest of any model; Opus 5.5’s is 50%.
Intelligence Index: 50, 5 points below GPT-6.1 Sol.
Theo’s blind code audit: 47 of its 92 claims were false.

models.rationale: A, last: Agent Arena (#8, +10.6% on Nov 4) puts it with the tier, and AA’s Intelligence Index v5 scores it 50, level with Muse Wonder Full and 5 below GPT-6.1 Sol. AA-Omniscience v1.1 gives it the lowest hallucination rate of any model (4%). Held at the bottom of A by Theo’s blind audit (3.95, with half its checked claims false), #10 in Code Arena WebDev and Epoch’s 6th place on software engineering. Google’s best generally available model: Gemini 4 Carbon (Oct 28) is stronger but reaches only selected users (see notShown). On Nov 9 AA’s v5 posts replaced its Sep 30 Intelligence Index v4.3 post (53, and a 15% hallucination rate on AA-Omniscience v1).

models.name: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017

points.text: #3 open-weights model in Agent Arena, behind Kimi K3.1 Pro.
Intelligence Index: 33, to Kimi K3.1 Pro’s 46.
FrontierCode merge-ready code test: 28.5%, to GPT-6.1 Sol’s 40.6%.

models.rationale: B: a cheap, usable open-weights model: #3 among open-weights models in Agent Arena (+2.2%, #22 overall on Nov 4), behind Kimi K3.1 Pro, whose weights came out on Nov 4, and MiMo-V2.6-Pro; 33 on AA’s Intelligence Index v5 at $0.60 a task (x.com/ArtificialAnlys/status/2119854348587123007); 28.5% on FrontierCode 2.0, the best open-weights score when AA launched it on Oct 28. Not S Chores: GPT-6.1 Sol leads it on every reviewed test. Kimi K3.1 Pro is stronger (Agent Arena +5.1%, Intelligence Index 46) but outside the major labs; DeepSeek holds its lab’s slot. Grok 4.7 now edges it in Agent Arena (+2.7% vs +2.2%), on the Intelligence Index (35 vs 33) and on FrontierCode 2.0 (28.7% vs 28.5%) at over ten times the cost per Intelligence Index task, so the tiers stand. Arena labels it DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (Max) on both Nov 4 boards and names the same #3 open-weights entry DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-20261017 (Max) on Nov 9 (x.com/arena/status/2119840698614817076). On Nov 9 the first point was rewritten (Kimi’s weights are out), the Intelligence Index points moved to v5, and DeepSeek’s own DeepSWE chart and Arena’s Oct 19 debut post left its posts.

models.name: Grok 4.7

points.text: Coding-agent index: 47, to GPT-6.1 Sol’s 54.
FrontierCode merge-ready code test: 28.7%, to GPT-6.1 Sol’s 40.6%.
Theo: unacceptably bad frontend; it gets stuck in loops.

models.rationale: F: shown because it is xAI’s latest model, but a cheaper shown model beats it on converging independent evidence: GPT-6.1 Sol leads it in Agent Arena (+12.5% vs +2.7% on Nov 4), on FrontierCode 2.0 (40.6% vs 28.7%), on AA’s Coding Agent Index v2.0 (54 vs 47) and on its Intelligence Index v5 (55 vs 35). DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 no longer beats it (Grok edges it in Agent Arena and on both AA tests) but costs over ten times less per Intelligence Index task. AA’s matched-effort gains over Grok 4.6 are real but do not close the gap to Sol. On Nov 9 FrontierCode 2.0 replaced 1.1 (33.8% vs Sol’s 49.1%).

notShown.note: Two generations behind: Agent Arena +6.1% against GPT-6.1 Sol’s +13.6% (Oct 24). Dropped at Kirill’s request; no reviewed source prefers it.

notShown.note: AA’s Sep 22 Coding Agent Index had it two points above GPT-6 Luna (43 vs 41), a single result, not widespread preference. Dropped at Kirill’s request.

notShown.name: Grok 4.6
notShown.note: Rechecked Oct 21: AA’s matched-xhigh Coding Agent Index v1.5 rises from 47 to 56 with all three components up. Theo’s complaints about 4.7 also call 4.6 slower and less pleasant; no widespread preference for 4.6.

notShown.name: Sonnet 5.5
notShown.note: Rechecked Nov 9: #3 in Agent Arena at +15.4% (Nov 4), 4.6 points behind Opus 5.5 and ahead of GPT-6 Astra (+14.5%). Behind Opus 5.5 on AA’s Intelligence Index v5 (55 vs 59), FrontierCode 2.0 (41.7% vs 46.4%), the Coding Agent Index v2.0 (59.3 vs 61.7), Code Arena WebDev (1806 vs 1769) and Theo’s audit (8.40 vs 7.88); it led only the Coding Agent Index v1.5 and Terminal-Bench 4.0 (64% vs 60%). Not a Chores pick: AA measured the highest cost per coding task of any model, $14.19.

notShown.name: Fable 5.1
notShown.note: Fable 5.2 improves on it on AA’s Intelligence Index v5 (65 vs 49) and FrontierCode 2.0 (49.1% vs 31.6%) at a 20% lower price per token. Agent Arena #5 at +13.4% (Nov 4), which has not rated Fable 5.2 yet; no reviewed source prefers 5.1.

notShown.name: Mythos 5.2
notShown.note: Released Nov 9 with Fable 5.2 as the same model under lighter cyber and biology safeguards, only for organizations in Anthropic’s Life Sciences and Cyber Verification Programs (anthropic.com/claude-fable-and-mythos-5-2). No independent evaluation, and most readers cannot get it.

notShown.name: GPT-6 Astra
notShown.note: On the chart until Nov 9, in A’s spare slot. Still strong: #4 in Agent Arena at +14.5% (Nov 4), 57 on AA’s Intelligence Index v5, 42.4% on FrontierCode 2.0 and 54.7 on the Coding Agent Index v2.0, ahead of GPT-6.1 Sol on quality. When Fable 5.2 entered S, the seven slots went to the three S models and each other major lab’s best; GPT-6.1 Sol is OpenAI’s value pick at about a sixth of Astra’s Agent Arena cost per task ($0.89 vs $5.16, x.com/arena/status/2115820547619926144).

notShown.name: GPT-6.1 Terra
notShown.note: Released Oct 26 (x.com/OpenAI/status/2114780720170164735). Cheaper per task than GPT-6.1 Sol but behind it in Agent Arena (+10.9% vs +12.5% on Nov 4), on AA’s Coding Agent Index v2.0 (48 vs 54, x.com/ArtificialAnlys/status/2114781869179031785) and on its Intelligence Index v5 (51 vs 55); ahead on FrontierCode 2.0 (42.3% vs 40.6%). Mixed, so Sol keeps S Chores.

notShown.name: Gemini 4 Carbon
notShown.note: Released Oct 28 only to cyber defenders in Google’s Fairwind Program, with wider access “coming soon” (x.com/Google/status/2115489522603466766); AA calls it not yet publicly available. Strong: #2 in Agent Arena at +16.5% (Nov 4), 60 on AA’s Intelligence Index v5, 59 on its Coding Agent Index (x.com/ArtificialAnlys/status/2115494553780367384) and 40.6% on FrontierCode 2.0. Place it once Google opens general access; it would likely take Gemini 4 Argon’s slot.

notShown.name: GPT-6 Luna
notShown.note: Rechecked Oct 21 and kept over GPT-5.6 Luna. Cheapest useful OpenAI model (Agent Arena’s frontier below $0.10 a task), but far behind GPT-6.1 Sol: Agent Arena +2.8% vs +13.6% (Oct 24), FrontierCode 41.9% vs 49.1%.

notShown.name: Haiku 5.5
notShown.note: 41.8% on FrontierCode and 43 on AA’s Intelligence Index; GPT-6.1 Sol at medium effort scores higher on AA for $0.21 a task. Not a Chores pick.

notShown.name: Muse Wonder
notShown.note: Meta’s API model. Behind Muse Wonder Full in Agent Arena (+3.3% vs +10.7% on Oct 24), Code Arena WebDev (1651 vs 1726) and AA’s Coding Agent Index v2.0 (52 vs 58.9).

notShown.name: Muse Spark 1.3
notShown.note: AA: Muse Wonder Full improves on it in all ten Intelligence Index evaluations (48 to 56). Agent Arena +3.1% (Oct 24).

notShown.name: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash
notShown.note: The 1017 build gains six points on AA’s Intelligence Index and 52 points in Code Arena WebDev; Agent Arena +2.3% vs +4.4% (Oct 24).

notShown.name: MiMo-V2.6-Pro
notShown.note: AA has it one point above DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 (46 at $0.13 a task) and 45.4% on FrontierCode, but it trails in Agent Arena (+3.3% vs +4.4% on Oct 24) and Code Arena WebDev (1626 vs 1664). Mixed against DeepSeek, and well behind GPT-6 Astra for the spare slot; over the seven-model limit.

notShown.name: Kimi K3.1 Pro
notShown.note: Released Oct 23 (x.com/Kimi_Moonshot/status/2113680701770068067); weights published Nov 4 (x.com/Kimi_Moonshot/status/2118010528123773297). The #1 open-weights model in Agent Arena (#13 overall at +5.1% on Nov 4, x.com/arena/status/2118088183594541527), 46 on AA’s Intelligence Index v5, the best open-weights score, and 67% on Terminal-Bench 4.0, the best of any model; 25.5% on FrontierCode 2.0. Strongest model outside the six major labs, but DeepSeek holds its lab’s slot and no spare slot is left; over the seven-model limit.

notShown.name: Kimi K3
notShown.note: Kimi K3.1 Pro improves on it in Agent Arena (+7.6% vs +1.6% on Oct 24), Code Arena WebDev (1692 vs 1655) and AA’s Intelligence Index (55 vs 44).

notShown.name: MiniMax-M3.1-Flash
notShown.note: Open weights since Oct 23. Intelligence Index 42 (x.com/ArtificialAnlys/status/2112211865128608002) and Code Arena WebDev #32 (x.com/arena/status/2112156275282968930): behind DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 on both; over the seven-model limit.

notShown.name: Muse Spark Open
notShown.note: Meta’s open-weights model, Oct 15 (x.com/AIatMeta/status/2110779754274292212). Intelligence Index 39 (x.com/ArtificialAnlys/status/2110893784422908225) against Muse Wonder Full’s 56; not on Agent Arena.

notShown.name: Muse Ember
notShown.note: Meta’s smallest model, released Nov 9 on Meta’s API (x.com/AIatMeta/status/2119853591703998787). 36 on AA’s Intelligence Index for $0.14 a task and 46 on its Coding Agent Index in Muse Code (x.com/ArtificialAnlys/status/2119854348587123007), against Muse Wonder Full’s 50 and 58.9; not on Agent Arena yet.

notShown.name: Hy4
notShown.note: Tencent’s model, proprietary until its weights are released. #14 in Agent Arena at +4.7% (Nov 4, x.com/arena/status/2117878267504103555), 35 on AA’s Intelligence Index v5 and 31% on FrontierCode 2.0 (x.com/ArtificialAnlys/status/2118259055546482834): behind Kimi K3.1 Pro and outside the major labs; over the seven-model limit.

notShown.note: Code Arena WebDev #12 (1672) and 43.2% on FrontierCode for the 0902 build; no Agent Arena or independent coding-agent result for the current build.

sources.caveat: Agents are model plus harness. v2.0 scores run lower than v1.5 for almost every configuration (mean 54.8 to 47.4 across the 21 measured on both), so the two versions don't compare. The DeepSeek entry is V4.1 Flash, not the 1017 build. Costs are API costs, not subscription prices.

sources.summary: Theo calls Grok 4.7 a disappointing release: poor frontend and 3D results, repeated loops, and worse usability than he expected. He also describes Grok 4.6 as slower and less pleasant than 4.5, while allowing that 4.7 can be pleasant on some engineering tasks.
sources.caveat: Firsthand qualitative evaluation without a named harness, task set, or effort setting. His complaints conflict with AA’s measured coding gains. Cost/token assertions are context, not independently reproduced measurements or tier weights.
